title: Пуля для Нагиева  (A Bullet for Nagiyev)

segments.t: When the prop master admits he has no real bullet tip for Nagiyev to hold in his mouth, Nagiyev snaps at him to make one out of anything—while at the housewarming, Kostya brings out his store-bought sausage.
Стоп, мне же еще в рот ее брать!
Я последний раз такое делал очень давно.
Я ужас как люблю эту еду.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'I catch the bullet with my teeth!' Dmitry Nagiyev anchors the line on 'I', while 'with teeth' completes the thought.
'Awesome, go bring a bullet!' The grammar packs 'caliber' and 'bring' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'We do not have a bullet.' Notice how Russian expresses 'at' and 'path' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Dmitry Nagiyev answers right away.
'Then make a bullet quickly.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'so' before landing on 'quickly'.
'What am I supposed to make it out of?' The meaning hinges on 'from' working together with 'will do' in spoken Russian.
'What difference does it make to me out of what?' Dmitry Nagiyev raises the pitch on 'what' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Chef Barinov answers right away.
'Fine, I will make it right now.' The grammar packs 'all right' and 'will do' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Стоп, мне же еще в рот ее брать!
'Wait, I still have to put it in my mouth!' In Russian, the idea of 'stop' flows naturally into 'to take' without extra filler words.
Я последний раз такое делал очень давно.
'The last time I did something like this was a very long time ago.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'for a long time'.
Я ужас как люблю эту еду.
'I terribly love this food.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'food'.
'I completely forgot about the sausage!' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'sausage' without extra filler words.
'I will slice it for the table right now.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'now' before landing on 'table'. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Стоп, мне же еще в рот ее брать!
Я последний раз такое делал очень давно.
Я ужас как люблю эту еду.
Placing a plate of ordinary supermarket sausage in front of Nastya's meat-factory-owner father sets off an explosive argument. See you in the next scene.
